ORDER
PER HON’BLE MR. VIRENDER BHAT, JUDICIAL MEMBER
1. The instant appeal, in which the above mentioned two
applications have been filed which are being disposed of by this
order, pertains to the establishment of the 400/220 kV GIS
Ambernath (District Thane) intra-state transmission project
(hereinafter referred to as “Ambernath Project”) envisaged in the
Empowered Committee meeting dated 8th July, 2025 and approved
by the Government of Maharashtra vide order dated 3rd October,
2025 to mitigate the demand growth in Thane region of the State for
the benefit of large pool of general consumers.
2. The Appellant has, in this appeal, assailed the order dated 1st
June, 2026 passed by the 1st Respondent – Maharashtra Electricity
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IA Nos. 1385 & 1664 of 2026 Page 2 of 19

Regulatory Commission (hereinafter referred to as “the Commission”)
in case No. 88 of 2026 whereby the Commission has allowed the
development of Ambernath sub-station project under the Distribution
Framework - Dedicated Distribution Facility (DDF) by Respondent
No. 4 and has permitted the recovery of Operation and Maintenance
(O&M) charges by 3rd Respondent – Maharashtra State Electricity
Transmission Limited (MSETL).
3. We may note that prior to passing of the impugned order dated
1st June, 2026, the Commission vide order dated 26th May, 2026 had
granted approval to the exclusion of Ambernath sub-station project
from Tariff Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB) framework.
4. The facts in brief which have led the Appellant to file the instant
appeal and which are relevant for the disposal of the captioned
applications are :-
i. Government of Maharashtra, vide order dated 4th January,
2019 constituted an Empowered Committee for the
construction and development of intra-state transmission
project in the State of Maharashtra. In the meeting held on 8th
July, 2025, the Committee discussed the appointment of Bid
Process Coordinator for conducting bidding process for
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IA Nos. 1385 & 1664 of 2026 Page 3 of 19

identifying and selecting entities for implementation of such
transmission projects.
ii. Vide subsequent order dated 3rd October, 2025, the
Government of Maharashtra inter alia appointed REC Power
Development and Consultancy Limited (in short REC-PDCL) to
act as bid process coordinator in relation to the Ambernath
Project. Accordingly, REC-PDCL issued a single stage
Request for Proposal (RFP) dated 8th December, 2025 for the
purpose of selection of bidder as transmission service provider
through competitive bidding process to develop the intra-state
transmission project for establishment of 400-220 kV GIS
Ambernath Project.
iii. Bids were invited by REC-PDCL from prospective stake
holders for undertaking the construction and development of
Ambernath project. Both Appellant and Respondent No. 4
participated in the bidding process in terms of the RFP dated
8th December, 2025. In all, six bidders had participated and
qualified for the opening of initial price offers after technical
evaluation. Subsequently, four bidders qualified for
participation in the e-Reverse Auction conducted on MSETC
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IA Nos. 1385 & 1664 of 2026 Page 4 of 19

portal during the period from 2nd April, 2026 to 10th April, 2026
with a ceiling price of Rs.1250 million. During the e-Reverse
Auction process, the discovered tariff was approximately
Rs.0.20 million which was found to be abnormally low,
unrealistic and commercially unviable in comparison to the
base price and prevailing market condition.
iv. Accordingly, in view of Clause7.5 of the TBCB Guidelines dated
10th August, 2021 issued by Ministry of Power, Government of
India which empowered the bid evaluation committee to reject
bids not aligning with the prevailing market prices, the bid
process for the project was annulled by the bid process
coordinator in its meeting dated 23rd April, 2026. This was
communicated to the Appellant on 29th April, 2026.
v. It appears that in the meanwhile, Respondent No. 4 vide letter
dated 6th April, 2026 addressed to 2nd Respondent, offered to
develop the Ambernath project free of cost and reiterated the
said proposal vide subsequent letter dated 8th May, 2026.
vi. The Empowered Committee, in its 10th Meeting held on 12th
May, 2026 considered the failure of TBCB process and taking
into consideration the strategic importance of the project as well
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IA Nos. 1385 & 1664 of 2026 Page 5 of 19

as the proposal of Respondent No. 4 to bear entire capital
expenditure and O&M expenses without any tariff implication
on the consumers, recommended implementation of the project
under the DDF framework subject to the approval of the
Commission.
vii. On the basis of said recommendations of the Empowered
Committee, the MSTU vide letter dated 22nd May, 2026 sought
Commission’s approval for the implementation of the project
under the DDF framework. As noted hereinabove, the
Commission vide letter dated 25th May, 2026, granted approval
for exclusion of the project from TBCB.
viii. Accordingly, MSTU approched the Commission by way of case
No. 88 of 2026 seeking approval of the development of the
proposed 400-220 kV GIS Ambernath sub-station under the
DDF framework and for recovery of O&M expenses from
Respondent No. 4. The petition was disposed of by the
Commission vide the impugned order dated 1st June, 2026.
5. Feeling aggrieved by the said order of the Commission, the
Appellant, which was one of the bidders who had submitted bids for
the project in pursuance to the RFP dated 8th December, 2025 and
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IA Nos. 1385 & 1664 of 2026 Page 6 of 19

had qualified for participation in the e-Reverse Auction, has
approached this Tribunal by way of the instant appeal.
6. We may note that when the appeal had come up for hearing
before this Tribunal for the first time on 25th June, 2026, the Learned
Senior Counsel, Mr. Sanjay Sen appeared for the Appellant and
pressed for ad interim relief as sought in IA No. 1385 of 2026.
Accordingly, we heard the Learned Senior Counsel and upon
considering his submissions, by an ad interim order, we directed that
the impugned order of the Commission shall remain in abeyance and
shall not be acted upon.
7. Upon receipt of notice of the appeal, the Respondent Nos. 2, 3
& 4 have filed their replies to IA No. 1385 of 2026. A separate
application bearing IA No. 1664 of 2026 has also been filed on behalf
of Respondent No. 4 seeking vacation of the ex-parte ad interim order
dated 25th June, 2026.
8. We have heard Mr. Tabrej Malawat, Learned Counsel for the
Appellant, Mr. Nikhil Nayyar, Learned Senior Counsel for the
Commission - 1st Respondent, Mr. B.P. Patil, Learned Senior Counsel
for the 3rd Respondent and Mr. C.S. Vaidhyanathan and Mr. Sajan
Poovayya, Learned Senior Counsels for 4th Respondent.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IA Nos. 1385 & 1664 of 2026 Page 7 of 19

9. We have also gone through the written submissions filed on
behalf of the parties.
10. The case of the Appellant is that it had emerged as L-1 bidder
in the competitive bidding process and, therefore, neither the TBCB
exclusion order dated 26th May, 2026 nor the impugned order ought
to have been passed in the absence of the Appellant and without
hearing it. It was further argued by the Appellant’s counsel that
MSTCU had no power to convert the intra-state transmission project
into DDF and the same is in violation of power conferred upon it vide
Government order dated 4th January, 2019. Learned Counsel further
sought to argue that the Commission too had no legal power to
convert the Ambernath Project from Section 63 of TBCB route to
DDF. It is argued that the Ambernath project is not eligible to be
implemented under DDF framework as it is not a distribution project
but an EHV intra-state transmission project. Thus, it is argued that
once the Appellant emerged as the lowest bidder and was declared
successful bidder on 10th April, 2026, the entire bidding process could
not have been annulled on 29th April, 2026 paving way for illegally
converting the transmission system into DDF project at the instance
of Respondent No. 4. Learned Counsel urged that the ad interim
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IA Nos. 1385 & 1664 of 2026 Page 8 of 19

order dated 25th June, 2026 may be made absolute till the disposal of
the appeal.
11. On behalf of the Respondents, it is vehemently argued that the
Appellant has misled this Tribunal by stating that the Appellant was
declared the successful bidder on 10th April, 2026. It is submitted that
the ex-parte ad interim order dated 25th June, 2026 has been
obtained by the Appellant on the basis of such false mis-
representation. It is pointed out that the bid process coordinator had,
at no point of time declared Appellant or any other bidder as L-1 or
the successful bidder and accordingly no Letter of Award (LoA) was
issued to the Appellant during or after the e-Reverse Auction process.
Learned Senior Counsel for Respondents would argue that in terms
of the powers under Recital 11 read with clause 2.5.6 (o) and 2.17 of
the RPF, bid process coordinator was empowered to annul bidding
process prior to declaration of any successful bidder without
assigning any reason and without any liability. It is argued that in the
absence of any formal declaration of Appellant as the successful
bidder and in the absence of any LoA/LoI issued in its name, no
vested right whatsoever accrued in favour of the Appellant and,
therefore, the entire challenge of the Appellant to the impugned order
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IA Nos. 1385 & 1664 of 2026 Page 9 of 19

of the Commission must fail. It is further pointed out that Regulation
15 read with Annexure IV of MERC MYT Regulations, 2004 permit
the implementation of intra-state transmission system above the
threshold limit of Rs.200 crores through cost plus mechanism under
Section 62 of the Electricity Act with prior approval of the
Commission. According to the Learned Senior Counsels, the
Appellant in the instant appeal is actually but indirectly challenging
the validity and legality of annulment of TBCB process and such
challenge is not maintainable before this Tribunal. On these
submissions, it is urged that the ad interim order dated 25th June,
2026 may be vacated forthwith.
12. We have considered the rival submissions advanced by the
Learned Senior Counsels and perused the record.
13. At the very outset, we are constrained to note that the Appellant
appears to have obtained the ex-parte ad interim order dated 25th
June, 2026 in this appeal by mis-representation of facts. Manifestly,
it was a malafide attempt on the part of the Appellant to mislead this
Tribunal by presenting false facts in order to extract the ad interim
order from this Tribunal.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IA Nos. 1385 & 1664 of 2026 Page 10 of 19

14. On 25th June, 2026, while advancing submissions on the
interim application, Learned Senior Counsel for the Appellant
contended that the Appellant had emerged as the lowest bidder in the
bidding process and was declared a successful bidder on 10th April,
2026. To substantiate these contentions, Learned Counsel for the
Appellant during the hearing on 5th August, 2026 produced a print-out
of the computer screen of the web portal on which the bidding process
was going on, which bears the date of 10th April, 2026 and mentions
L-1 below the name of the Appellant. It is on this basis that the
Appellant claims to have been declared successful L-1 bidder on the
said date i.e. 10th April, 2026. However, it is to be noted that this was
only a system generated bid flow message which is displayed solely
for the purpose of indicating the current bidding position/status of a
bidder during the on-going action process on a particular date. Such
message is provisional and dynamic in nature and is subject to
change on the basis of subsequent bids and system validations. All
the bidders in e-Reverse Auction process can see “my status” link
during the course of bidding process to check their respective status
as to whether they are the L-1 bidder at a given point of time on a
particular date. We note at the cost of repetition that the position
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IA Nos. 1385 & 1664 of 2026 Page 11 of 19

changes dynamically as the bidding progresses. It appears that the
Appellant herein has taken a screen shot of the said link, which is
exclusively for private viewing of a particular bidder and is not
concurrently visible to all the bidders.
15. The fact remains that concededly the bidding process had not
concluded as no communication was addressed by the bid process
coordinator to the Appellant intimating it that it has emerged as
successful L-1 bidder. After conclusion of each bid event, a bid sheet
is generated and made available for public view which is considered
confirmatory and authoritative with respect to bid ranking and the
outcome of the bid. As regards the bidding process in question, no
such confirmatory and authoritative bid sheet was issued by the bid
process coordinator.
16. Therefore, it is evident that in the absence of any such
confirmation from the bid process coordinator, the Appellant falsely
claimed itself to have emerged as a successful L-1 bidder in the
bidding process and succeeded in obtaining an ex-parte ad interim
order from this Tribunal on 25th June, 2026 on the basis of such
deliberate false representation.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IA Nos. 1385 & 1664 of 2026 Page 12 of 19

17. As contended on behalf of the Respondents, since the last bid
received on 10th April, 2025 was for the sum of Rs.0.20 million which
was abnormally low as compared to base price and also was
commercially unviable, the BPC rightly realized that the subsequent
bids would be lower than it and therefore, there was no point in
continuing the bidding. Accordingly, the empowered Committee in its
10th meeting held on 12th May, 2026 decided to annul the entire
bidding process.
18. The Appellant does not dispute that neither was any
communication sent to it by BPC stating that the bidding has come to
an end in which appellant has emerged successful L-1 bidder nor was
any LoA/LoI issued to him. Mere fact that the portal, on which bidding
was going on, showed appellant as L-1 on a particular day i.e.
10.04.2026 when the bidding was in progress without being formally
concluded nowhere indicates that the Appellant was a successful
L-1 bidder. The bidding event was annulled prior to its conclusion and
before issuance of any confirmatory bid sheet as the lowest bid
submitted was found too low and unviable. Thus no right, more so a
vested right, had got vested in favour of the Appellant.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IA Nos. 1385 & 1664 of 2026 Page 13 of 19

19. All these facts have been mischievously concealed by the
Appellant in the Appeal as well as in the application for interim relief.
It is a settled principle that a person seeking equitable relief of interim
stay must approach the court with clean hands. However, the
Appellant herein has founded its appeal on false and distorted facts
in an endeavour to mislead this Tribunal. Thus, Appellant is not
entitled to such equitable relief of interim stay as sought in the IA No.
1385/2026 and the ad-interim order dated 25th June, 2026 is liable to
be vacated on this very score.
20. The contention on behalf of the Appellant that the entire bidding
process could not have been annulled as the bid process coordinator
was not empowered to do so, also is devoid of any merit. On this
aspect, we may refer to the Tariff Based Competitive Bidding
guidelines for transmission service dated 10th August, 2021, Clause
7.5 of which is as under :-
“7.5 The bidder with the lowest annual transmission
charges discovered after the e-reverse bidding procedure
will be considered for the award. The Evaluation
Committee shall have the right to reject all price bids if the
rates quoted are not aligned to the prevailing prices.”
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IA Nos. 1385 & 1664 of 2026 Page 14 of 19

21. Thus, it is clear that the bids could be rejected if the rates
quoted are not aligned with the prevailing prices, which exactly has
happened in this case, and therefore, no infirmity can be found in the
decision to annul the bidding process.
22. On this aspect, the relevant clauses of the RPF document,
which are extracted hereinbelow, are also material and need to be
referred to :-
“11. The RFP document is not transferable. BPC
reserves the right to reject all Bid and/or annual the
process of tariff based competitive bidding for selection of
Bidder as TSP to execute the Project without assigning
any reason. BPC shall not bear any liability, whatsoever,
in this regard.”………………………………………………...
…………………………………………………………………
2.5.6 Bidders may note that :-
j) If for any reason the Bid of the Bidder with the lowest
Quoted Transmission Charges is not selected or Letter of
Intent issued to such Selected Bidder is cancelled or such
Bidder withdraws its Bids, the BPC may :-
i. Invite all the remaining Bidders to revalidate or
extend their respective Bid Security, as necessary, and
match the Bid of the Bidder with the lowest Quoted
Transmission Charges (the "second round of bidding")
with following cases:
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IA Nos. 1385 & 1664 of 2026 Page 15 of 19

• If in the second round of bidding, only one Bidder
matches the Bid of the Bidder with lowest Quoted
Transmission Charges, it shall be the Selected Bidder.
• If two or more Bidders match the Bid of the Bidder with
the lowest Quoted Transmission Charges in the
second round of bidding, then the Bidder whose
Quoted Transmission Charges was lower as compared
to other Bidder(s) in the first round of bidding shall be
the Selected Bidder. For example, if the third and fifth
lowest Bidders in the first round of bidding offer to
match the Bid of the Bidder with lowest Quoted
Transmission Charges in the second round of bidding,
the said third lowest Bidder shall be the Successful
Bidder.
• In the event that no Bidder offers to match the Bid of
the Bidder with the lowest Quoted Transmission
Charges in the second round of bidding, the BPC may,
in its discretion, invite fresh Bids (the "third round of
bidding") from all Bidders except the Bidder which
quoted the lowest Quoted Transmission Charges in the
first round of bidding. In case the Bidders are invited
for the third round of bidding to revalidate or extend
their Bid Security, as necessary, and offer fresh Bids,
they shall be eligible for submission of fresh Bids
provided, however, that in such third round of bidding
only such Bids shall be eligible for consideration which
are lower than the Quoted Transmission Charges of
the second lowest Bidder in the first round of bidding;
or;
ii. Annul the bid process; or
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IA Nos. 1385 & 1664 of 2026 Page 16 of 19

iii. Take any such measure as may be deemed fit in the
sole discretion of the BPC……………………………………
…………………………………………………………………
o) BPC reserves the right to reject all Bids and/or annul
the process of tariff based competitive bidding for
selection of Bidder as TSP to execute the Project without
assigning any reason. BPC shall not bear any liability,
whatsoever, in this regard. ………………………………….
…………………………………………………………………
“2.17 Right of the BPC to reject any Bid
BPC reserves the right to reject all or any of the Bid/s or
cancel the RFP without assigning any reasons
whatsoever and without any liability.”
(Emphasis supplied)
23. These clauses of the RfP document clearly indicate that the
BPC was within its rights to reject the bids or cancel the bidding
process at any stage without furnishing any reason or explanation for
the same. In the instant case, the BPC has even furnished the reason
for annulment of the bidding process, as already noted herein above.
24. One more aspect of the case which is material and needs to be
noted. Vide communication dated 29.04.2026, the Appellant was
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IA Nos. 1385 & 1664 of 2026 Page 17 of 19

informed that the bid process has been annulled and bid bonds in the
sum of Rs.4,93,00,000/- (Rupees Four Crores, Ninety Three Lakhs
only) submitted by Appellant were returned to it as having been
discharged. Thus, evidently the Appellant got knowledge upon receipt
of this letter that the bidding process has been annulled. Intriguingly,
Appellant has not challenged such annulment of bidding process
before any Court till date. Hence, he shall be taken to have accepted
such annulment and is precluded from challenging the impugned
order of the Commission which is subsequent to such annulment.
25. Thus, in the light of the above discussion, we conclude that the
appeal as well as the application bearing I.A. No. 1385 of 2026 of the
Appellant is founded upon false and concocted facts. The Appellant
has misled the Tribunal by knowingly presenting a fabricated and
fictious version of events in order to obtain a favourable order. In view
of the actual chain of events that has taken place which came to light
during the course of arguments on these applications, the Appellant
has failed to make out a prima facie case in its favour. Balance of
convenience too lies heavily in favour of the respondents and against
the Appellant. No loss or prejudice would be caused to the Appellant
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IA Nos. 1385 & 1664 of 2026 Page 18 of 19

in case of denial of interim relief as sought by way of IA No. 1385 of
2026 as no vested right has accrued in its favour.
26. Hence, the IA No. 1385 of 2026 is hereby dismissed. The ex-
parte interim order passed on 25th June, 2026 stands vacated.
Consequently, the IA No. 1664 of 2026 filed by the 4th Respondent
stands allowed.
Appeal No. 279 of 2026
27. In view of the detailed order passed on the IA Nos. 1385 of
2026 and 1664 of 2026, we feel doubtful about the maintainability of
the present appeal.
28. Accordingly, we post the appeal for arguments on the aspect of
maintainability on 12th October, 2026.
Pronounced in the open court on this 19th day of August, 2026.
(Virender Bhat) (Seema Gupta)
Judicial Member Officiating Chairperson
